headline: Government says its 'Your First Home' equity loan scheme will be confirmed in the October Budget
detail: On 26 September the government said the new homebuying equity loan scheme would be confirmed in next month's Budget, according to Reuters. The FT reported that the scheme revives Help to Buy, with the stated aim of boosting housebuilding.

headline: US President Trump rejects Iran's proposal for a week-long ceasefire to reopen the Strait of Hormuz
detail: The FT reported on 26 September that Tehran had offered a one-week pause in hostilities to start peace talks on the seven-month conflict. Reuters later reported that Iran still wants a diplomatic solution and that mediators had not formally passed on a US rejection.

headline: PM Burnham says social care reform will be funded by new taxes and put to voters at the next general election
detail: On 27 September, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said his plan for a national care service would be free at the point of use, with the cost shared across the population through new taxes. He said the reform would be hard to deliver in the current parliament, and the next election may not come until 2029.

headline: Chancellor Healey says UK capital gains tax is the lowest of any major European economy, ahead of the October Budget
detail: Chancellor John Healey made the comment on Sunday 27 September while discussing business confidence and competitiveness on capital taxes, City AM reported. The report said the remarks raise the prospect of another capital gains tax increase at the Budget.

headline: Chancellor Healey to set out a £6bn Royal Navy plan in his Labour conference speech
detail: The FT reported that the Chancellor will pledge that British firms will build three new floating docks on the Clyde as part of a £6bn Royal Navy plan. The speech is due on Tuesday.

headline: UK Business Secretary calls a possible US diesel export ban a significant concern; UK gets about a sixth of its diesel from the US
detail: US President Trump said he is seriously considering a diesel export ban, with a 90-day ban or more limited voluntary restrictions reported to be under consideration. UK Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds said a full ban would be a significant concern for Britain but noted that UK fuel supply is diverse.

headline: Oil rises more than 1% after Trump rejects Iran proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz
detail: A wire reported that oil prices climbed more than 1% after US President Trump rejected Iran's peace proposal. US stock futures were reported slightly lower.

headline: FT reports the Bank of England's balance sheet has grown over the past year despite quantitative tightening
detail: The Financial Times reported on 28 September that the Bank of England's balance sheet has stopped shrinking and is larger than it was a year ago. The report gave no figures.

headline: Brent trades above $106 a barrel as 10-year US Treasury yields reach 5.2%, adding pressure on government bonds
detail: The Financial Times reported early on 28 September that Brent was above $106 a barrel and 10-year Treasury yields had reached 5.2%. Wire headlines also reported higher Japanese government bond yields, citing concerns over the Iran conflict and inflation.

headline: BoE MPC member Dhingra flags concern that elevated interest rates could weigh on investment and reduce supply capacity
detail: Bank of England external MPC member Swati Dhingra said she is concerned that high rates could damage business investment and cut the economy's supply capacity, according to a newswire headline on 28 September. The inputs report no market reaction.

headline: ONS publishes revised Labour Force Survey series adjusted with PAYE data, showing a larger recent fall in employment
detail: The ONS has reworked its Labour Force Survey data using HMRC PAYE figures to correct for the drop in survey responses since the pandemic. The revised series shows a deeper fall in employment early in the pandemic, a stronger recovery afterwards and a bigger decline in recent months.

headline: Defence Secretary Streeting signals further defence spending announcements in the October Budget
detail: UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said more on defence spending will come at the Budget. He gave no figures.

headline: BoE's Ramsden says inflation risks have tilted to the upside and a Bank Rate rise could be warranted if pressures keep building
detail: BoE Deputy Governor Dave Ramsden said the current policy stance remains restrictive, and named energy prices, food prices and wage settlements as his main focus. He said he does not expect further QE to be considered soon, and described the QT plan and its September changes as credible and well received by markets.

headline: BoE's Ramsden says Bank's gilt sales will start with the longest maturities, reported as 2033 to 2049
detail: Deputy Governor Dave Ramsden said the Bank of England's gilt sales will begin at the long end of the maturity range. One report gave the range as 2033 to 2049 and another as 2035 to 2049. In the same remarks he said he wanted QT pushed further into the background and that a period of higher, longer-lasting headline inflation is shaping his thinking.

headline: US crude futures rise more than 4% to a session high of $96.44 a barrel as US-Iran peace efforts stall
detail: US crude futures rose more than 4% to a session high of $96.44 a barrel after peace talks between the US and Iran stalled.

headline: Global bond sell-off deepens as Brent rises above $108 and 10-year US Treasury yield tops 5.2%
detail: The FT reports that Brent crude has climbed above $108 a barrel and the 10-year US Treasury yield has passed 5.2% as hopes of a US-Iran deal fade. The latest snapshot shows the 10-year gilt yield at 4.602% and the 30-year at 5.329%.

headline: Chancellor Healey pledges to meet the fiscal rules and says fiscal discipline will be at the core of his Budget
detail: In his Labour conference speech, Chancellor Healey said the government will stick to its fiscal rules and keep control of the public finances. He called current debt levels an affront to the party's values and said the government must act to cut the welfare bill.

headline: UK diesel prices hit a record 199.18p per litre, according to RAC data
detail: City AM reported on 28 September that RAC figures showed diesel reaching a record 199.18p per litre. The report said UK borrowing costs were also rising ahead of the Budget.

headline: Chancellor Healey tells Labour conference there is no spare money for extra public service spending
detail: In his Labour conference speech on 28 September, the Chancellor said the public finances have less room than in the Blair years because growth is lower and debt is higher. The FT reported that the speech was preparing the party for possible tax rises in the Budget.

headline: US and Iran to hold separate talks with Qatari mediators, with no US officials at Iran's New York meeting
detail: An official told Reuters that Qatari mediators are expected to meet Iranian Foreign Minister Araqchi in New York and the US side separately on Monday or Tuesday. Iran's ISNA reported that no US representatives will attend Araqchi's meeting.

headline: Citi/YouGov: UK public year-ahead inflation expectations rise to 4.5% in September, long-term measure up to 4.3%
detail: The Citi/YouGov survey puts UK year-ahead public inflation expectations at 4.5% in September, compared with 3.9% previously. The longer-term measure rose to 4.3% from 4.1% in August.

headline: ECB's Lagarde says the inflation outlook for 2027 and 2028 is higher than expected and backs a measured policy response
detail: In a speech to the European Parliament, ECB President Lagarde said the inflation shock is too large to look through and that a measured response is appropriate. She said she sees no sign yet that inflation is becoming embedded, and that risks remain to the upside for inflation and to the downside for growth.

headline: ECB's Lagarde puts rates at the upper end of the neutral range as traders cut October hike odds below 40%
detail: ECB President Lagarde said euro area rates are at the upper end of the neutral range but that policy is not being set by reference to the neutral rate. Market pricing reported on 28 September showed less than a 40% chance of an ECB rate rise in October.

headline: PM Burnham says the defence investment plan will be fully funded at the Budget; social care funding details due tomorrow
detail: Prime Minister Burnham said in an LBC Radio interview on 28 September that the defence investment plan will be fully funded at the Budget. He also said details of social care funding will be published the following day.

headline: UK 10-year gilt yield rises to 5.441%, its highest level since July 2007
detail: A market newswire reported on 28 September that the 10-year gilt yield had climbed to 5.441%, the highest since July 2007. The move came as the global bond sell-off continued.

headline: US 10-year Treasury yield climbs 10bp to 5.27%; 2-year hits 4.952%, highest since May 2024
detail: Market newswires reported on 28 September that the US 10-year Treasury yield had risen by 10bp to 5.27%. The 2-year yield reached 4.952%, its highest since May 2024.

headline: US official says Trump is prepared to ease Iran sanctions and release frozen assets in return for nuclear progress
detail: A US official told Al Jazeera on 28 September that indirect talks with Iran through intermediaries are positive, but no deal is possible unless the nuclear issue is addressed. None of the posts reported a market reaction.

headline: Al Hadath reports Iran agrees to suspend uranium enrichment for US sanctions relief; US source puts deal chances as extremely slim
detail: Al Hadath, citing sources, reported that Iran has agreed to halt uranium enrichment in exchange for easing of US sanctions. Shortly afterwards, a US source involved in the negotiations told Al Arabiya that the gaps remain wide and the chances of an agreement are extremely slim, and Iranian officials were separately reported to be pessimistic about a deal before the US midterms.

headline: Saudi Arabia resumes oil exports via East-West pipeline at about 3.5m bpd as US crude gives up gains near $92
detail: Sources said Saudi Arabia has resumed oil exports through the East-West pipeline after repairs, with Aramco running it at a throughput of around 3.5 million barrels a day. US crude was reported to have reversed its earlier gains and to be trading near $92 a barrel.

headline: Fed's Cook sees broadening US inflation pressure from AI and the Middle East conflict, and warns rate cuts could fuel inflation
detail: Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook said in a speech on 28 September that she sees signs of broadening pressure in inflation data and expects continued inflation pressure in the coming months from AI-driven demand and the Middle East conflict. She said lowering rates to offset any AI-related rise in unemployment could fuel inflation, and that future rate adjustments will depend on inflation and labour market data.

headline: Brent crude settles up 96 cents at $105.28 a barrel; WTI closes at $92.60
detail: Brent futures ended 28 September 0.92% higher at $105.28 a barrel, while NYMEX WTI November futures settled 19 cents higher at $92.60. NYMEX diesel settled at $4.7553 a gallon and natural gas at $3.00/MMBtu.

headline: Trump again threatens to ban US diesel exports to bring down domestic prices
detail: Semafor reported on 28 September that the US president repeated his threat to halt diesel exports from the US, the world's largest diesel producer and exporter. Separately, he said the US would win the Iran war very soon and that fuel prices would then fall sharply.

headline: Italian and French 10y10y forward yields rise about 10bp in a single session as the long end sells off
detail: A market economist reported on 28 September that 10-year-10-year forward yields for both Italy and France had risen by around 10bp during the day. No gilt market reaction was given.

headline: Iranian official denies reports that Iran has softened its nuclear stance and says no nuclear talks are under way
detail: Fars News reported an Iranian official as saying Iran's nuclear position is unchanged and that reports of flexibility are wrong. Separately, Al Jazeera reported that a new Iranian proposal puts off nuclear commitments until a first phase is implemented, and a senior Iranian security committee official said the Strait of Hormuz, not the nuclear issue, is now the focus of negotiations.

headline: Iran's parliament considers a bill to leave the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty, Fars reports
detail: Fars News cited an Iranian lawmaker as saying parliament is weighing a bill for Iran to exit the NPT. No timing for a vote was given.

headline: Iran's foreign minister says Qatari mediators will take Tehran's proposals to the US and hopes for a final US reply by Tuesday
detail: Iranian state news agency IRNA reported that Foreign Minister Araqchi said the Strait of Hormuz will reopen only if the supreme leader's conditions are met. Separately, President Trump said he had not given Iran any sanctions relief.

headline: Trump denies offering Iran sanctions relief or frozen funds and calls the Axios report untrue
detail: On Truth Social, President Trump said he had offered Iran nothing and demanded that Axios withdraw its report that he had offered sanctions relief and the release of frozen funds. His denial came as the US 10-year Treasury yield stood at levels last seen in 2007, with the sell-off attributed to faltering US-Iran diplomacy and concerns about oil prices.

headline: UK mortgage approvals fall to 54,918 against 56,100 expected; mortgage lending £4.41bn
detail: Bank of England data showed mortgage approvals below the 56,053 previous reading and the 56,100 forecast. Net mortgage lending was £4.410bn against £4.4bn expected (previous revised to £4.082bn), and M4 money supply rose 0.4% after -0.3%.

headline: ECB's Kazimir says rate hike was unavoidable and January repricing will be key, with energy prices still a major factor
detail: ECB Governing Council member Kazimir also stressed the need for flexibility and said there is plenty of time.

headline: EU energy commissioner tells US counterpart that restricting energy flows helps no one; Irish minister calls diesel ban unlikely
detail: The EU energy commissioner said the message was sent to the US following threats of a US diesel export ban. Ireland's energy minister said such a ban would significantly affect the EU but did not appear likely to happen.

headline: IEA's Birol says Europe gets 50% of its diesel from the US and further strategic reserve releases would be discussed if needed
detail: The International Energy Agency's executive director said Europe is among the regions most exposed in the diesel market and that the agency is in talks with countries about the situation.

headline: Iran's parliament speaker warns no regional state will sell oil if Iran cannot, and says regional infrastructure would not be safe
detail: Parliament speaker Qalibaf made the remarks according to Iranian state media. Separately, an IRGC spokesperson said the US has no option but to admit failure and leave the region.

headline: Spanish September flash CPI rises to 4.9% y/y against 4.6% expected; HICP at 5.0%
detail: Spain's flash CPI rose to 4.9% y/y in September from 4.3% (forecast 4.6%), and 0.3% m/m against 0.1% expected. HICP was 5.0% y/y (forecast 4.9%, previous 4.6%) and core CPI 3.1% y/y (forecast 3.0%, previous 2.9%).

headline: Brent crude futures rise more than 2% to $107.44 a barrel; December contract at $99.87
detail: Brent front-month futures gained over 2% in Asian trading to $107.44 a barrel, with the December contract also up more than 2% at $99.87.

headline: RBA raises cash rate 25bp to 4.60% as expected and says further tightening may be needed as Middle East conflict lifts energy prices
detail: The Reserve Bank of Australia raised its cash rate target from 4.35% to 4.60%, its third hike this year, in line with forecasts. It said inflation remains elevated, upside risks have emerged and energy prices far exceed its August forecast, and that it will raise rates further if needed. The Australian dollar rose to $0.7026 after the decision.

headline: US-Iran war adds €100bn to EU fuel bill, FT reports as bloc's energy ministers meet in Dublin
detail: The Financial Times reports a warning that the US-Iran conflict has added €100bn to the EU's fuel bill. EU energy ministers are meeting in Dublin.

headline: EU declares full solidarity with Estonia over attack blamed on Russia; Lavrov says Europe is waging war on Russia
detail: An EU spokesman said the bloc stands in full solidarity with Estonia after an attack attributed to Russia. At a press conference, Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov responded to Western claims of Russian hybrid warfare by saying Europe is waging war against Russia.

headline: Italy's energy minister to ask US Energy Secretary about a possible US diesel export ban on Tuesday
detail: Italy's energy minister said he would speak with US Energy Secretary Wright later on Tuesday and raise a possible US ban on diesel exports.

headline: UKMTO receives late report of vessel struck by projectile in Strait of Hormuz on 28 September
detail: UK Maritime Trade Operations received a late report that a vessel was hit by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz on 28 September.

headline: Iranian army offers 10bn toman reward for capture of any American soldier
detail: An Iranian army spokesperson announced a reward of 10bn toman to any Iranian who captures an American soldier, dead or alive. Separately, Qatar's foreign ministry said it is still passing messages between the US and Iran.

headline: UK sells £4.25bn of 10-year gilts at 5.383% average yield, highest for newly issued 10-year debt since 1999
detail: The morning 10-year gilt auction raised £4.25bn at an average yield of 5.383%, a reporter noted. That is the highest yield on new 10-year issuance since 1999. Secondary market yields were higher in 2007, but no 10-year gilts were issued that year.

headline: BRC survey shows shop price and food inflation easing in September while pipeline cost pressures build
detail: The British Retail Consortium's September shop price survey showed overall shop price inflation and food inflation both easing. The BRC said retailers still face rising cost pressures. The post gave no figures.

headline: UK consumer credit rises £2.464bn, above £1.9bn forecast and £2.006bn previously
detail: Bank of England figures put net consumer credit at £2.464bn, against a forecast of £1.9bn and £2.006bn in the previous month.

headline: North Sea Forties crude loadings are set at eight cargoes for November
detail: This is the published November loading programme for the Forties crude grade.

headline: US to allow Iraqi Airways to fly Iranian pilgrims to and from Najaf as US-Iran peace talks resume
detail: Iraqi officials say the US will let Iranian travellers fly to and from Najaf. Separately, Reuters reports that major Gulf stock markets were mixed as investors weighed renewed diplomatic efforts to end the US-Iran conflict.

headline: IEA's Birol warns Europe faces a very difficult winter and says another oil stock release is not a priority
detail: The IEA executive director said he hopes Europe and its allies will cooperate to limit energy risks. He said a further release of oil stocks is not at the top of the agenda.

headline: Trump backs Russia sanctions relief tied to a prisoner release, The Atlantic reports
detail: The Atlantic reports that President Trump expressed support for the plan a few months ago. It says the initiative is still at an early stage.

headline: EU energy commissioner rules out an EU-wide windfall tax and says any such levy should be set nationally
detail: The commissioner also said that, given current market conditions, taxes on electricity should be lower than taxes on gas.

headline: ECB's Escriva says policy is not yet restrictive and flags concern over the global rise in long-term rates
detail: Governing Council member Escriva said the ECB is not in restrictive territory, that the global upward path of long-term rates could add pressure on interest rates and that high energy prices could become anchored in inflation. He said he sees no second-round effects so far and that Spain is not considering moving its gold reserves.

headline: Putin envoy Dmitriev holds talks with US Treasury and Energy officials on ending the Ukraine war and on energy cooperation
detail: A US official described Monday's meeting in Washington as constructive and said the talks covered possible US-Russia energy initiatives once the war ends. Sources say Dmitriev met representatives of the US Treasury and Energy departments.

headline: Union leader warns PM Burnham against ending the pensions triple lock before his first conference speech
detail: The FT reports that a senior union leader said scrapping the triple lock would be electorally damaging. The warning came ahead of the Labour leader's first party conference speech as prime minister.

headline: Italy completes the withdrawal of its troops from Iraq
detail: A market newswire reported on 29 September that Italy has completed the withdrawal of its troops from Iraq.

headline: Wells Fargo Investment Institute lifts its end-2027 forecasts for the Fed funds rate and the 10-year Treasury yield
detail: The institute now forecasts the Fed policy rate at 4.75%-5.00% by the end of 2027, up from 4.00%-4.25%. Its forecast for the 10-year US Treasury yield rises to 5.25%-5.75%, from 4.50%-5.00%.

headline: Average UK diesel price reported to be close to £2 per litre, with the level expected within days
detail: A market newswire reported on 29 September that the average UK pump price of diesel is set to hit £2 a litre within days. The post gave no current price.

headline: Russian economy minister Reshetnikov is to attend a G20 meeting in the US, Interfax reports
detail: Interfax reported on 29 September that Russian Economy Minister Maxim Reshetnikov will take part in a G20 meeting being held in the United States.

headline: Netanyahu says there are signs Israel's enemies may try attacks ahead of elections and warns Israel can strike anywhere
detail: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on 29 September that there are indications of possible attacks on Israel as its elections approach. He said Israel is able to strike its enemies at any place and time.

headline: Canadian GDP is flat in July, in line with forecasts, after 0.3% growth in June
detail: Statistics Canada's monthly GDP for July came in at 0.0% m/m, matching the 0.0% consensus. The previous month's reading was 0.3%.

headline: Oman's OQ considers buying two supertankers for floating storage and plans to more than double Duqm oil storage
detail: Oman state energy company OQ SAOC is reported to be evaluating buying two supertankers to lease out for floating storage at the port of Duqm. Oman also plans to more than double oil storage capacity at Duqm.

headline: US VP Vance says Washington believes Iran's Supreme Leader is alive and that Iran must behave for any deal
detail: US Vice President JD Vance made the remarks on 29 September, as US-Iran peace talks resume. He said Iran's conduct is a condition for any agreement.

headline: NATO's Rutte accuses Russia of a reckless campaign of hostile acts against allies and pledges more support for Ukraine
detail: The NATO secretary general spoke at a joint press conference with Lithuania's prime minister and said Russia is failing.

headline: Merz and five other EU leaders threaten to block the EU's next seven-year budget without large spending cuts
detail: The FT reports that the German chancellor and five other leaders want spending cuts running into hundreds of billions of euros as a condition of agreeing the budget.

headline: Zelenskiy says Russia attacked two foreign ships in the Odesa area
detail: Ukraine's president said Russian forces struck two foreign vessels near the Black Sea port of Odesa.

headline: South Korea says North Korean mines caused a DMZ blast that broke the armistice and calls for talks
detail: South Korea's defence minister said last week's blast injured two South Korean personnel, warranted a response and that Seoul will urge Pyongyang to hold talks to verify the facts.

headline: Rubio says a foreign state was involved in the incident near a UK airbase used by US forces to strike Iran
detail: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said a foreign actor was involved in the incident, in which five men were arrested on suspicion of explosives and terrorism offences, Reuters reported.

headline: Estonia blames Russian sabotage for an arson attack on a defence company
detail: An Estonian minister attributed the arson attack on the defence firm to Russia.

headline: EU energy ministers to meet in October on winter energy security; Irish minister says Europe's reserves are ample
detail: Ireland's energy minister said EU countries can make temporary tax changes to ease high energy costs and that ministers will discuss winter supply at an October meeting.

headline: IEA's Birol says member states may discuss further strategic oil reserve releases if needed
detail: On Tuesday the head of the International Energy Agency said member countries could consider releasing more strategic oil stocks onto the market in future, Reuters reports.

headline: BoE money and credit data show UK broad money growth holding at around 4%
detail: The Bank of England's money and credit release published this morning shows broad money growth staying subdued at roughly 4%.

headline: Kremlin says its decrees putting foreign firms' Russian units under temporary control will not change their ownership
detail: The Kremlin said the temporary administration decrees bring in external management and are partly a response to unfriendly countries' growing military involvement against Russia. It called the move reversible but said there are currently no grounds to reverse it. In the same briefing it denied involvement in the arson attack on an Estonian defence company and said it wants Iran to remain in the nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty.

headline: Lufthansa says its extra jet fuel bill this year will exceed the €1.5bn flagged in August
detail: Lufthansa's chief executive said higher oil prices during the Iran war will push the airline's additional jet fuel costs above the €1.5bn estimate it gave in August, Reuters reports.

headline: Saudi Arabia resumes oil loadings at Red Sea port of Yanbu after East-West Pipeline restarts
detail: Trade sources and shipping data show that Saudi Arabia has restarted loadings at Yanbu after bringing the East-West Pipeline back into operation, Reuters reports.

headline: RBA raises cash rate by 25bp to 4.60%, its fourth increase this year
detail: The Reserve Bank of Australia's Monetary Policy Board raised the cash rate target by 25bp to 4.60% at its meeting overnight. This is the fourth hike in 2026.

headline: PBOC cuts PSL rates by 25bp to 1.5% for 1-year and raises relending quotas by a combined 700bn yuan
detail: The People's Bank of China lowered pledged supplementary lending rates by 0.25 percentage points, taking the 1-year PSL rate to 1.5%, and changed several other policy tools. Relending quotas rise by 500bn yuan for agriculture and small businesses and by 200bn yuan for technology upgrades, and China will help cover interest payments on first-time home mortgages.

headline: Vessel is struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz on 28 September, UK maritime authorities report
detail: The UK Maritime Trade Operations centre said it had received a late report of an incident in Hormuz, in which a vessel was hit by a projectile on 28 September.

headline: Iran says it sent a seven-point plan to the US via Qatar and is awaiting an official reply
detail: Iran's foreign minister said Tehran's seven-point plan had been passed to Washington through Qatar and that Iran is waiting for a formal US response.

headline: Iranian army offers a 10bn toman reward for capturing a US soldier as IRGC calls Trump a liar
detail: An Iranian army spokesperson announced the reward for capturing an American soldier, dead or alive. Separately, a Revolutionary Guards spokesperson accused the US president of hiding the truth about Iran's nuclear programme and the effect of Iran's blockade of Gulf energy supplies.

headline: Italy's energy minister is to raise a possible US diesel export ban with the US Energy Secretary on Tuesday
detail: Italy's energy minister said he will speak with US Energy Secretary Wright later on 29 September and will ask about a potential US ban on diesel exports.

headline: Putin bans individuals from taking more than 1m roubles in cash out of Russia to neighbouring countries
detail: The Kremlin published a decree barring cash exports above 1m roubles to EAEU countries, Azerbaijan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan, with certain exceptions.

headline: EU Court of Justice rejects Poland's bid to suspend provisional application of the EU-Mercosur trade deal
detail: The EU Court of Justice dismissed Poland's application to suspend the EU Council decision authorising provisional application of the EU-Mercosur agreement.

headline: Senior union leader warns the UK PM against ending the pensions triple lock at Labour conference
detail: The Financial Times reported that a senior union leader told the prime minister at the Labour conference that scrapping the state pension triple lock would be electorally reckless.

headline: ECB's Escriva says policy is not yet restrictive and flags concern over rising global long-term rates
detail: ECB Governing Council member Escriva said euro area policy is still not in restrictive territory. He said the upward trend in long-term rates worldwide worries him and could put pressure on interest rates.

headline: US-Iran war adds €100bn to EU fuel bill as energy ministers meet in Dublin, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports the warning that the conflict has added €100bn to the EU's fuel costs. It was issued as the bloc's energy ministers meet in Dublin.

headline: EU energy commissioner rules out an EU-wide windfall tax and says any such levy should be set nationally
detail: The EU energy commissioner said there are no plans for a bloc-wide windfall tax and that any such tax is better set at national level. The commissioner added that, in current market conditions, taxes on electricity should be lower than those on gas.

headline: EU declares full solidarity with Estonia after an attack blamed on Russia
detail: An EU spokesman said the bloc stands in full solidarity with Estonia after an attack that has been blamed on Russia.

headline: US official says Putin envoy Dmitriev held constructive talks with US officials on ending the war in Ukraine
detail: According to a US official, Dmitriev met US officials on Monday to discuss a peaceful settlement of the war in Ukraine and possible US-Russia energy initiatives once the war ends.

headline: IMF projects a $54bn funding gap for Ukraine by 2029, reports say
detail: Reports say the IMF expects Ukraine to face a financing shortfall of $54bn by 2029.

headline: Qatar says it is passing messages and possible solutions between the US and Iran as talks continue
detail: A spokesman for Qatar's foreign ministry said meetings are ongoing and that Qatar is relaying messages between the American and Iranian sides. The spokesman also accused the Netanyahu government of repeatedly trying to undermine Gaza ceasefire efforts.

headline: Union leader warns PM Burnham that ending the pensions triple lock would be electoral insanity
detail: According to the FT, a senior union leader gave the warning before the Prime Minister's first party conference speech as Labour leader. The Resolution Foundation and NIESR have both published calls to replace the triple lock.

headline: ECB's Escriva says high energy prices could become embedded in inflation but sees no second-round effects so far
detail: Bank of Spain Governor and ECB Governing Council member José Luis Escrivá said elevated energy prices might anchor in inflation, but that second-round effects are not yet visible. He also said Spain is not considering moving its gold reserves.

headline: Putin envoy Dmitriev meets US Treasury and Energy Department officials in Washington, reports say
detail: According to sources cited in reports, including Tass, Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev met representatives of the US Treasury and Energy Departments in Washington. The reports say this followed talks with Kushner and Witkoff in New York.
